summary: In this episode of Tafseer Surat Al-Anbiya, Sheikh Ali Mashhour discusses the Quranic references to Gog and Magog (Yajuj and Majuj), focusing on distinguishing authentic Islamic descriptions from fabricated narrations. He explains that according to authentic hadith and scholarly consensus, Gog and Magog are human beings, descendants of Adam, who are extremely numerous and morally decadent with inclinations toward violence and warfare. Sh. Ali Mashhour critiques weak and fabricated narrations that describe them as tiny creatures or possessing monstrous features, tracing these descriptions back to biblical and fables rather than authentic Islamic sources. He employs historical examples to illustrate how human societies naturally exaggerate and demonize their enemies when lacking proper chains of transmission, comparing this to how ancient Greeks and Persians described each other and how modern nations have similarly distorted enemy descriptions. The lecture concludes that while it remains theoretically possible that Gog and Magog remain behind their wall, it is more probable they are among scattered nations throughout earth who possess modern technology while maintaining their violent nature.
